title: Genetics and crop planning — controlled evidence plan
purpose: Define genetics intake, crop scheduling, capacity and identity controls while preserving genotype-by-environment uncertainty and lot genealogy.

excludedUntilValidated: guarantee that cultivar name predicts phenotype
plant-count decisions that ignore facility/legal capacity
assumption that one environment expresses every genotype the same way

claims.statement: Cannabis phenotype and production performance emerge from genotype interacting with environment and management, so crop plans should preserve genetic identity without assuming a cultivar name guarantees one fixed outcome.
claims.boundary: Genetic naming alone does not establish authenticity, stability, flowering duration, yield or chemistry.

claims.statement: Seed, clone and stock-source records should preserve supplier/source, cultivar or line identity, lot/batch, date received and propagation relationship so later performance can be traced to the correct genetics.
claims.boundary: A label is only useful when identity controls prevent mix-ups and undocumented relabeling.

claims.statement: Crop scheduling should incorporate biological readiness and observed development rather than treating planned calendar dates as proof that a crop is ready to move stages.
claims.boundary: The SOP should not universalize one vegetative or flowering duration across genotypes and environments.

claims.statement: Unexpected sex expression can occur and may have genetic, developmental and environmental contributors, so flowering plans should include reproductive scouting and an escalation pathway.
claims.boundary: No single stressor or cultivar label should be presented as a universally predictive cause of intersex expression.

claims.statement: Planned plant counts, room occupancy and turnover should be reconciled against actual survival, readiness, spacing and facility capacity so schedules do not hide biological or operational variance.
claims.boundary: Facility/legal plant-count limits and occupancy requirements remain locally controlled.

claims.statement: Crop records should preserve planned versus actual dates, room/zone, genotype, batch genealogy, losses, substitutions and deviations so later review can distinguish genetic, timing and process effects.
claims.boundary: Retrospective schedule changes must not erase the original plan or make the crop appear to have followed it exactly.
